originality.rationale: The closest published theorem classifies near-perfect numbers with exactly two distinct prime factors, not by total multiplicity, and the focal 2022/2023 paper says the general even classification is open. The closest published-finding corpus near-perfect item is a 2-adic shape theorem for n congruent to 2 mod 4; it does not imply the complete Omega<=4 list. A second published-finding corpus hit concerns 2-near-perfect numbers, a different definition. The present theorem also proves that 234 and 650 are the only three-support cases in the low-multiplicity boundary.
residual_risks: A differently phrased low-total-multiplicity classification could exist outside the searched literature and databases; no such statement was located in the focal or closest primary papers.
OEIS is used only as a witness table and not as novelty or exhaustiveness evidence.

value.rationale: Classifying all even near-perfect numbers is open. Total prime-factor multiplicity is a natural complexity measure independent of distinct-prime support. The theorem closes the entire first four multiplicity layers and identifies the exact point at which three-prime support first appears, giving a finite, reusable boundary result rather than a numerical cutoff.
